episodes.206773: Remnant moisture from two tropical cyclones, Priscilla and Raymond moved into the state of Arizona.  Two west coast troughs interacted with this remnant moisture and provided ample lift and shear for heavy rain and severe thunderstorms.  The rain led to creek and stream level rises and some flash flooding.
episodes.207225: A surge of moisture brought flash flooding to southern Utah.
episodes.207378: A rapidly deepening low pressure system off the Carolina Coast interacted with strong high pressure ridging centered in the Northeast which extended down into the Mid-Atlantic. As these two systems interacted, a tight pressure gradient resulted allowing for storm force wind gusts across the Eastern North Carolina Coastal Waters and the Pamlico Sound during the overnight hours of October eleventh through the morning hours of October Twelfth.
episodes.207558: A shallow, lower tropospheric boundary moving southward from the southeast Gulf of America waters in the wake of an earlier cold frontal passage was the focus for convective shower development.  A brief waterspout was reported near Big Coppitt Key.
episodes.207895: Tropical moisture from the remnants of Pacific Hurricane Priscilla plus an approaching trough in the westerlies fueled scattered thunderstorms, a few of which produced flash flooding.
episodes.207909: An influx of tropical moisture from tropical storms Pricilla and Raymond allowed for deep moisture as well as showers and thunderstorms to form from October 11th through October 14th. Severe thunderstorms moved through the Tucson Metro area on October 11th causing multiple reports of 1 inch hail and uprooted trees on the southeast side of the metro. Additionally, as this storm moved northward caused damage to electrical equipment causing a power outage to 856 customers for 18 hours. Multiple rounds of light to locally heavy rainfall on September 12th caused washes to run with water in the Tucson metro causing 9 swift water rescues with no injuries. Additionally, there were multiple reports of a funnel cloud near Drexel Heights. On October 13th there was an isolated thunderstorm and showers that caused flow in washes through October 14th. This led to a swift water rescue in Eloy with no injuries. The 4 day rainfall totals ranged from 0.5 inches to locally up to 4.0 inches.
episodes.207934: A nearly stationary upper-level trough combined with tropical moisture remnants from Tropical Storms Priscilla and Raymond, which developed off the eastern Pacific, led to scattered to widespread thunderstorm activity across much of south-central AZ. Beginning late on the 8th through the 9th, very anomalous moisture from Tropical Cyclone Priscilla surged northward with PWATs rising to over 1.5+, which was an all-time record for early October. Light to moderate rainfall developed, with the most widespread activity occurring from the afternoon of the 10th into the early afternoon of the 11th. Even though rainfall rates were light with no flooding occurring with this initial activity, it saturated the soils for the heavy rainfall that would develop hours later. ||Heading into the pre-dawn hours on the 12th, another moisture surge, this time from the remnants of Tropical Cyclone Raymond, combined with strong upper-level ascent from the aforementioned low pressure system off the west coast to trigger scattered thunderstorm activity across much of south-central AZ during the morning and early afternoon hours. With MLCAPE values having increased to around 1000 J/KG, the environment was conducive to high rainfall rates in excess of 1-2+ an hour. These high rainfall rates falling on top of saturated soils resulted in numerous instances of flash flooding across much of south-central AZ. ||Another round of scattered thunderstorm activity developed during the afternoon hours on the 13th. With MLCAPE values peaking at 1000 J/KG and deep-layered shear values approaching 50 kts, the environment became conducive for the development of severe thunderstorms, including supercells. One such supercell affected the Chandler, Tempe, and Scottsdale areas with the city of Tempe being severely hit with extensive wind damage from large, mature trees uprooted or snapped, some of which damaged buildings and vehicles, to downed powerlines, and roofs blown off buildings. A damage survey conducted by some NWS Phoenix Meteorologists supported wind gusts with this supercell peaking around 80-90 mph. Other storms that developed through the afternoon and early evening resulted in large hail and more instances of flash flooding. By the end of the multi-day event, rainfall totals ranged between 1.00-1.50��� across the Phoenix West Valley to as high as 3.50-4.50��� across the Phoenix East Valley, with locations across the foothills and higher terrain areas observing total amounts of 2.50-6.00���.
episodes.208102: A board upper-level and secondary trough feature dropping southward from Canada in addition to cold air aloft supported convective activity. Some of this strong shower and thunderstorm activity was was unusually impactful producing locally severe outflow winds and a funnel cloud.
episodes.208337: A coastal low formed off of the Southeast coast on October 11 and slowly tracked north into October 13 before moving offshore. Meanwhile, a strong area of high pressure lingered over the Gulf of Saint Lawrence. This resulted in a prolonged period of strong northeast winds and Storm conditions across the coastal waters on October 12.
episodes.208407: Between October 10-14, 2025, southwest Colorado experienced prolonged periods of rain and some of the largest multiday rainfall totals on record with rainfall accumulations between 3 and 8 inches, with locally higher amounts across the San Juan Mountains. Remnants from two tropical storms supplied anomalous moisture across the region, with minimal break between events. The first round of heavy rainfall resulted in flooding across La Plata and Archuleta counties from decaying Tropical Storm Priscilla beginning October 10 and continuing throughout the day on the 11th. There was a break in rain across the area on October 12, followed by a second round of heavy rain from October 13-14, associated with moisture from remnant Tropical Storm Raymond. Without much time between systems, the hydrologic response of the second storm was much faster than the first. Flooding across several counties in southwest Colorado spiked twice within the 5-day window, leading to major flooding and near record peaks along the Vallecito, Piedra and San Juan watersheds that lingered through the 16th before water levels receded. Numerous debris flows and rockslides also occurred as a result of the abundant rainfall.

events.narrative: Wind gusts were recorded overnight between the eleventh and twelfth of October at Diamond Shoals Buoy. Max wind gust was recorded at 21:40 LT.

events.county: Nc-Va Bdr To Currituck Beach Lt Out 20Nm
events.narrative: Strong northeast winds developed due to a coastal low lingering offshore on October 12. The Duck Pier NOS site gusted to 40 to 50 knots between 1 AM and 12:30 PM EST on October 12 with a peak gust of 48 knots at 11:36 AM EST.
A flood wave of 1220 cfs was recorded on the East Fork of the Virgin River. A 450 cfs flood wave was recorded on the North Fork of the Virgin River.
Flash flooding washed out multiple water lines in Meadview overnight, leaving some customers without water until the next day.
Antares Road was closed from Highway 66 to Pierce Ferry Road due to flooding overnight.
Navajo Nation Highway Department reported, via Facebook, Navajo Route 9846 west of Dilkon was closed due to a washout.  Timing is estimated and location on map is estimated.
Wind gusts occurred during the early morning hours of October 12th with just over two hours of gusts above 48 knots. Report came in via WeatherFlow.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Stream Gauge located along Rainbow Wash near Highway 85 showed water levels rising above the alarm stage level of 1.3 feet and exceeding the bankfull level of 4.1 feet, peaking at 4.57 feet (2842 cfs). This resulted in all downstream low-water crossings to become flooded with several inches of flowing water. This included the old U.S. 80 near Patterson Road, where a water rescue was performed. Timing based on the stream gauge located along the wash. No injuries reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Stream Gauge along Waterman Wash at Rainbow Valley Road south of Buckeye reported water levels rising above the alarm stage level of 3.1 feet, with water levels peaking at 4.9 feet (1133 cfs).  A couple of water rescues were performed near the vicinity of the wash, one near Narramore Road and another near Tuthill Road. One of the flood incidents along the wash turned deadly as a man was found deceased after the pickup truck he was driving was washed away from the floodwaters. The pickup truck was found less than a mile downstream with the man not found, requiring a search and rescue operation to be activated. The body the man was eventually found by the search and rescue team approximately 34 hours after the reported incident. Timing was estimated based on radar and the nearby stream gauge.

Significant flooding originating from a culvert took down block walls and caused major property damage to 4-5 homes with water levels as high 1.5-2 feet in a neighborhood block located near the area Loop 202 and Broadway Road in East Mesa. No injuries reported.
Small bridge located in the area of Beverly Road and 133rd Avenue in Goodyear was washed away by the floodwaters. No injuries reported.
US-60 near Gilbert Road closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries reported.
Images showed 1.5 diameter hail in Anthem. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.

Radar indicated heavy rain between 0300 and 0400 MST. This heavy rain caused multiple mudslides to occur around 0400 MST between Carbondale and Redstone along Highway 133 centered around mile marker 55.7. Another one occurred at mile marker 53 within this similar timeframe. One vehicle was stuck in the mudslide but not buried. No indication of how deep or wide the slide was but clean up took longer than usual due to the stuck vehicle. Road reopened in both directions at 0917 MST.
Video showed 1 diameter hail near New River. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
A 1210 cfs flood wave was recorded on the Fort Pearce Wash gauge.
Water rescue performed along Estrella Parkway near Lum Wash. No injuries reported.
Water rescue due to flash flooding along West Dobbins Road near South 19th Avenue. No injuries reported.
US Route 17 was closed at Dock Street due to flooding.
Heavy rain caused mud and rockslides on Frying Pan Road in Pitkin County. Road closed at 511 MST and was reopened by 623 MST.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Stream Gauge along Skunk Creek Wash near Desert Hills Drive showed water levels rising above the alarm stage level of 2.22 feet, peaking at 2.46 feet (504 cfs), and making all low-water crossings downstream impassable. A water rescue was performed along North 19th Avenue, which is one of the low water-crossings.  Timing was estimated based on the period water levels exceeded and then receded below alarm stage level and when the water rescue incident occurred. No injuries reported.

Multiple social media images posted showed flooding around the Ak-Chin Village area. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Stream Gauge along Indian Bend Wash near Shea Boulevard in Scottsdale measured water levels rising above the alarm stage level of 2.0 feet, peaking at 2.17 feet (900 cfs), and likely making low-water crossings downstream impassable. Timing was estimated based on the stream gauge. No damages or injuries reported.
Roosevelt and Osborn Roads closed between Miller and Hayden Roads due to excessive water runoff on Indian Bend Wash in Scottsdale. No damages or injuries reported.

Video shared on the Maricopa County Flood Control District X page showed water flowing along 69th Avenue from Skunk Creek Wash in Peoria making the roadway impassable. No damages or injuries reported.
Kings Highway South at 24th Ave North shut down due to flooding  with at least one car stalled.

Six to eight inches of fast flowing water along East Apache Trail near North 88th street in Mesa. No damages or injuries reported.

Video shows a torrent of water moving down Latham Boulevard in Miami. No damages or injuries reported.
Road closures reported at 24th Ave N closed and Withers Drive due to flooding.

Video image showed a torrent of water moving down Pinal Creek and overtopping the bridge at East Haskins Road in Globe. No damages or injuries reported.

Railroad St was completely flooded.

The NWS Damage Assessment Team surveyed wind damage from a strong convective shower that moved through Longview, Washington around 3:13 PM PDT Oct. 12, 2025. Based on the wind damage, estimated peak winds of 80-85 mph occurred, most likely with a wet microburst that produced damaging straight-line winds over a small geographic area.

Broadcast media reported a funnel cloud associated with a strong rain shower around 3:53 PM PDT Oct. 12, 2025 in La Center, Washington. There were no reports of a tornado on the ground and/or wind damage with this cell.
Six inches of standing water was reported over E Calhoun St and covering up to apartment steps.
